# Psychological safety

## Summary

Psychological safety means people expect no punishment or embarrassment when they raise an idea, ask a question, voice a worry or admit a mistake. In a team, members feel free to take social risks without being made to look foolish. The article describes it as the most studied enabling condition in research on group dynamics and team learning.

## Why It Matters

The survey's "my team" section scored 74 favourable, but the item "I can raise a concern without fear" was 58 ([[engagement-survey-2026-results-summary]]). Reading this made me see that gap as the more interesting result. It also explains part of the anonymity debate: people answer honestly only when they trust the survey, which is [[gabriel-santoro]]'s point in the [[survey-reporting-threshold-decision-2026-06-10|threshold discussion]].

## Caveats

An overview; it does not say how to measure psychological safety in a single survey item.
